findings.evidence: Basic.lean:269-297 defines both maps plus `groupSchemeι_def`/`groupSchemeιGeneralLinear_def`; Basic.lean:301 and 322 give two `IsClosedImmersion` instances; `GeneralLinear/Determinant.lean` has no scheme-level determinant morphism (only `determinantCoordinateMap`, line 82).

findings.issue: Two public inclusions of the same closed subgroup now coexist, differing only by `eqToHom (GeneralLinear.groupScheme_def R n).symm`: `groupSchemeι` (raw `hopfSpec` target) and `groupSchemeιGeneralLinear` (named target), each with its own `IsClosedImmersion` instance. Downstream lemmas about `SLₙ ⊂ GLₙ` will fragment across the two names, and the determinant triangle already leaks a presentation `eqToHom` into its right-hand side (line 344).

summary: The new `SpecialLinear.schemePointsMulEquiv` exposes only a `symm` computation, and the missing forward lemma is compensated by `CommHopfAlgCat.transportPointwiseFormula`, a public 13-argument pure-`MulEquiv` scaffold in a Hopf-algebra namespace. Opacifying `groupScheme`/`groupSchemeι` also removed the kernel universal property from the named surface without restating it, and leaves two public inclusions of the same subgroup.
